avoid_supplements.name: Iron supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Famotidine increases gastric pH, reducing iron absorption by up to 50%
avoid_supplements.action: Separate iron supplementation by at least 2 hours from famotidine dosing

avoid_supplements.name: Calcium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Reduced stomach acid impairs calcium citrate absorption; calcium carbonate may also be affected
avoid_supplements.action: Take calcium supplements 2+ hours before or after famotidine; use calcium citrate formulation if possible

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin B12
caution_supplements.mechanism: Chronic famotidine use may reduce B12 absorption due to hypochlorhydria; typically only clinically significant with long-term use
caution_supplements.action: Monitor B12 levels if using famotidine chronically; consider supplementation if deficiency develops

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Elevated gastric pH may slightly reduce magnesium absorption
caution_supplements.action: No strict separation required, but monitor for adequate magnesium status with prolonged use

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Famotidine reduces gastric acid; caffeine may cause increased gastric irritation in some patients with underlying conditions
caution_foods.action: No restriction needed; counsel patients to monitor symptoms and reduce caffeine if heartburn worsens

caution_foods.name: Spicy, acidic, or fatty foods
caution_foods.mechanism: While famotidine reduces acid, these foods may still trigger symptoms in susceptible individuals
caution_foods.action: Encourage dietary modification based on individual symptom response

monitoring_notes: Famotidine has minimal drug metabolism and low interaction potential. Monitor for malabsorption of iron and calcium with concurrent supplementation; counsel patients on proper timing of supplements. Assess B12 status in patients on chronic therapy (>1 year).
